thread:
Anya: heads-up — seeing a TTFT p99 spike on the token-level dashboard for us-west2 starting ~13:05 UTC. tokens/sec drops as well :eyes:
Liam: can you paste the grafana panel link?
Anya: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ttft/token-latency-heatmap?orgId=1&var-region=us-west2  (heatmap shows narrow vertical band across many shards)
Maria: any node-level network counters? could be NIC noise. check `node_network_receive_errs_total` and `node_network_transmit_errs_total`
Josh: running a quick grep, one host looks noisy: `gpu-12-3.us-west2` shows rx_errors rising around 13:04. ifconfig shows `RX packets: 1.2M errors: 120 dropped: 0 overruns: 0 frame: 0`
Sam: alertbot just fired:
alertbot: Alert fired: `TTFT_p99_high` — p99 > 1.5s (5m) — region=us-west2 — impacted_shards=~18
Anya: confirmed alert. curious that tokens/sec (sum(rate(tokens_processed[1m]))) also dips at same time for the same shard set. suggests networking or NIC backpressure rather than model runtime slowdown
Liam: can we pull per-shard network IO heatmap + pod CPU wait? queries: `sum by(shard) (rate(tokens_processed[1m]))` and `irate(node_net_packets_total[1m])`
Maria: also check iface drops from `node_network_receive_errs_total` grouped by instance, and `eni_tx_err` for host-level cloud metrics
Josh: running `kubectl top pod -n inference --selector=shard in (s1,s2,s3) --containers` — CPU fine, memory fine. kernel tx queue backlog shows `netstat -s` with increasing `packet receive errors` on gpu-12-3
Anya: good catch. would explain token latency tail; if the kernel is dropping packets, some request streams block waiting on socket buffers, increasing TTFT p99 but median unchanged
Sam: suggestion: cordon + drain gpu-12-3 quickly, move shards to warm pool. fallback model variant is ready if capacity is tight (policy: region-fallback -> smaller-quantized variant) :thumbsup:
Liam: before draining, can we verify whether NIC driver rebind helps? ops-runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/network/nic-flaky.md (steps below)
Liam: ```
# quick check
ssh gpu-12-3
etstat -i
dmesg | tail -n 50
# if obvious driver errors, try rebind
echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:3b:00.0/remove
echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan
```
Maria: if we drain, autoscaler might spin up new nodes slowly — prefer to shift traffic by scaling up warm pool first then drain. I'll kick a manual scale to +3 in us-west2 warm group
Anya: good. Sam, can you own the drain? Liam, if you can try a rebind in parallel on gpu-12-3 (non-disruptive attempt)
Sam: on it. starting cordon now: `kubectl cordon gpu-12-3`
Josh: adding a short-term dashboard tweak: reduce noise by splitting p99 alerts by `instance` to avoid region-wide firing when single node noisy. propose alert change: `for: 10m` and `group_by: [instance, shard]`
Anya: agree. also add a grafana panel that overlays `node_network_receive_errs_total` with `TTFT_p99` for quick triage (small visual correlation panel)
alertbot: Note: `TTFT_p99_high` alert suppressed for 5m due to acknowledged action by Sam
Sam: drain complete, pods remapped, tokens/sec back to expected after ~70s. monitoring shows p99 dropping back under 1.2s
Liam: rebind attempt show kernel NIC resets in dmesg on gpu-12-3 — will file infra ticket to replace NIC on that instance after business hours
Maria: warm pool scaled +3, autoscaler logs show new nodes healthy in ~2m
Anya: follow-ups: (1) infra ticket for hardware replacement (2) tweak alert: split by instance/shard + longer for region-wide, (3) add overlay panel for quick correlation, (4) runbook note to prefer warm-pool scale before drain. I'll create GH issue for the dashboard + alert changes
Josh: assigning myself for the dashboard PR, will ping for review
Sam: good incident summary, posting to #incidents later. :white_check_mark:
